blocks.text: Understanding Apple Dictation vs Siri

When you look at Apple Dictation vs Siri, you are comparing a typewriter to a personal assistant. Apple Dictation is a tool for inputting text. You open a document, trigger the feature, and speak. It fills your cursor with words. It does not control your Mac or answer questions about the weather.

Siri is different. It is an assistant designed to perform actions. You ask Siri to set a timer, create a reminder, or open a specific app. While Siri now includes writing tools to help with tone or proofreading, its primary purpose is interaction and control.
How Apple Dictation Works on Mac

Apple Dictation is a system-level feature. It is always there, waiting for your keyboard shortcut. On most Macs, you trigger it by pressing a key or going to Edit > Start Dictation. It works in any field that accepts text. This includes browser search bars, Word documents, or Slack messages.

If you have a Mac with Apple silicon, the processing happens on your device. This is fast and works offline. It is also private, as your audio does not leave the machine. Intel-based Macs rely on server-side processing, which requires an internet connection.
What Siri Can Do for Your Mac Workflow

Siri has evolved into a more conversational assistant. It can now access context from your Photos, Mail, and Notes. If you need to find a document from last week, Siri is the tool to ask. It also handles system-wide actions, such as editing messages or adding songs to your music queue.
Siri AI is currently in beta. Some features like Visual Intelligence may show inconsistencies. Advanced capabilities are limited to newer Macs with specific hardware requirements.

blocks.text: When to Use Each Tool

Use Apple Dictation when you have a long block of text to write and you want to keep your hands off the keyboard. It is perfect for drafts, emails, and quick notes. It is simple, free, and built into your system.

Use Siri when you want to manage your Mac without clicking through menus. If you need to set a reminder for a meeting or check your calendar, Siri is efficient. It is also useful for quick facts or adjusting system settings.

Consider Lazur if you find yourself stuck on how to use an app. If you are looking for a specific menu item or want to know how a feature works, ask Lazur. It can point to the button or guide you through the process step by step.
Privacy Considerations

Privacy matters when you use voice tools. Apple Dictation on Apple silicon keeps your audio on your Mac. You can verify this in your Keyboard settings. Siri uses Private Cloud Compute for complex requests, ensuring that your data is not stored or accessible to Apple.

Lazur also prioritizes privacy. It only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the activation shortcut. It does not store your audio or screenshots, and it does not use your data to train models.

blocks.text: Getting Started with Voice Tools
To start with Apple Dictation, go to System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation and turn it on. Choose your language. Use the shortcut provided to begin speaking.
To use Siri, go to System Settings > Siri & Spotlight. Configure your preferred activation method. Once set up, you can start using it for your daily tasks.

faq.question: Is Apple Dictation free?
faq.answer: Yes, Apple Dictation is a free, built-in feature on all modern Macs.

faq.question: Can Siri replace Apple Dictation?
faq.answer: Not entirely. While Siri has writing tools, Apple Dictation is specifically optimized for continuous text entry.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Apple Dictation?
faq.answer: Lazur is a separate tool that includes its own dictation capabilities, but it does not replace the system-level Apple Dictation.
